performance_question: Does raising each of 24 cache-backed AIPerf clients' outstanding-request cap from 128 to 512 permit faithful delivery of the unchanged 12,106 RPS Mooncake schedule to one Envoy callout gateway?
reason_for_revision: At concurrency 128, all 24 clients were replay-degraded: one representative client completed 12,639 of 22,699 scheduled requests at 277 RPS, with mean latency 449 ms. Little's law gives about 124 in-flight requests, almost the 128 cap, so client concurrency was binding.

overrides.instrument.request_records: AIPerf 0.12.0 --export-level records, existing pinned mmap reader fix
overrides.quality_gates: 24 complete clients; zero errors/cancellations; all cache HIT; no replay-degraded clients; max p99 schedule lag 500 ms; profiling-start spread at most 3 seconds; retain request-level JSONL

comparison_limit: This is a new concurrency-control series. c128 was an invalid offered-load replay; use it only to diagnose client saturation. A valid c512 result, if any, characterizes one gateway under this load but does not by itself establish a hard ceiling.
